title: Customers without orders
description: Find every customer who has never placed an order.
code:
SELECT c.id, c.name
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
WHERE o.id = NULL;
issue_title: NULL comparison is wrong
issue_description: Using `= NULL` never matches, so customers without orders are not returned.
issue_suggestion: Use `IS NULL` when checking for NULL values.

title: Recent orders pagination
description: Return the 20 most recent orders for the dashboard.
issue_title: LIMIT without ordering is unstable
issue_description: Without `ORDER BY`, the query can return arbitrary rows instead of the most recent ones.
issue_suggestion: Sort by the timestamp before applying the limit.

title: Average order amount by customer
description: Show each customer with their average order amount.
issue_title: Non-aggregated column is missing from GROUP BY
issue_description: `customer_name` is selected but not grouped, which is invalid or nondeterministic depending on the database.
issue_suggestion: Add `customer_name` to the grouping columns.

title: Products with a given prefix
description: Search product names that start with the supplied prefix.
issue_title: Pattern matches anywhere, not just the prefix
issue_description: Wrapping the parameter on both sides finds substring matches instead of prefix matches.
issue_suggestion: Append the wildcard only on the right side.

title: Duplicate user emails
description: List email addresses that appear more than once.
code:
SELECT id, email, COUNT(*) AS duplicates
FROM users
GROUP BY id, email
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;
issue_title: Grouping by primary key hides duplicates
issue_description: Including `id` makes every row unique, so duplicate emails are never grouped together.
issue_suggestion: Group only by the email column.
issue_code:
SELECT email, COUNT(*) AS duplicates
FROM users
GROUP BY email
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;

title: Order totals by product
description: Calculate total revenue contributed by each product.
issue_title: Revenue formula is incorrect
issue_description: Revenue should multiply quantity by price, not add them together.
issue_suggestion: Multiply `quantity * unit_price` inside the aggregation.
issue_code: SELECT product_id, SUM(quantity * unit_price) AS revenue

title: Open tickets excluding resolved ones
description: Return all tickets that are still active.
issue_title: NULL statuses are silently dropped
issue_description: Rows with a NULL status do not satisfy `!= 'resolved'`, even though they are effectively unresolved.
issue_suggestion: Handle NULL explicitly if those rows should stay visible.
issue_code: WHERE status != 'resolved' OR status IS NULL;

title: Latest login per user
description: Show each user with their latest login timestamp.
issue_title: Selected column is not grouped
issue_description: `email` is selected without grouping or aggregation, which breaks the query shape.
issue_suggestion: Add `email` to the grouping columns if it is stable per user.

title: Customers and paid order counts
description: Show all customers with the number of paid orders they have.
code:
SELECT c.id, c.name, COUNT(o.id) AS paid_orders
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
WHERE o.status = 'paid'
GROUP BY c.id, c.name;
issue_title: WHERE clause turns the LEFT JOIN into an INNER JOIN
issue_description: Customers without paid orders disappear completely because the status filter runs after the join.
issue_suggestion: Move the paid-status filter into the JOIN condition.
issue_code: LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id AND o.status = 'paid'

title: Top spending customers
description: Return the five customers with the highest lifetime spend.
code:
SELECT customer_id, SUM(total_amount) AS spend
FROM orders
GROUP BY customer_id
ORDER BY spend ASC
LIMIT 5;
issue_title: Sort direction is reversed
issue_description: Ascending order returns the lowest spenders instead of the highest ones.
issue_suggestion: Sort the aggregated total in descending order.

title: Sessions older than 30 days
description: Delete session rows that expired more than 30 days ago.
code:
DELETE FROM sessions
WHERE created_at < NOW() - 30;
issue_title: Interval arithmetic is invalid
issue_description: Subtracting a bare integer from a timestamp is not portable and often invalid SQL.
issue_suggestion: Use an explicit interval expression.

title: Employees without managers
description: Find employees who do not report to anyone.
issue_title: NULL comparison is invalid
issue_description: `= NULL` never returns true, so root employees are missed.
issue_suggestion: Use `IS NULL` to test for absent manager IDs.

title: Items low in stock
description: Return inventory items that need a reorder soon.
issue_title: Rows with unknown thresholds are included incorrectly
issue_description: If `reorder_level` is NULL, the row is returned even though there is no threshold to compare against.
issue_suggestion: Require a real threshold before comparing quantity.
issue_code: WHERE reorder_level IS NOT NULL AND quantity < reorder_level;

title: Order count by day
description: Group orders into daily buckets for the chart.
code:
SELECT created_at, COUNT(*) AS orders_count
FROM orders
GROUP BY created_at
ORDER BY created_at DESC;
issue_title: Grouping by timestamp is too granular
issue_description: Grouping on the raw timestamp creates one bucket per distinct moment instead of per day.
issue_suggestion: Truncate the timestamp to a day before grouping.
issue_code:
SELECT DATE(created_at) AS order_day, COUNT(*) AS orders_count
FROM orders
GROUP BY DATE(created_at)
ORDER BY order_day DESC;

title: Users missing profiles
description: Find user accounts that do not have a related profile row.
code:
SELECT u.id, u.email
FROM users u
JOIN profiles p ON p.user_id = u.id
WHERE p.id IS NULL;
issue_title: Inner join makes NULL check impossible
issue_description: An inner join removes unmatched users before the NULL filter runs.
issue_suggestion: Use a LEFT JOIN when searching for missing related records.
issue_code: LEFT JOIN profiles p ON p.user_id = u.id

title: Inactive subscriptions
description: List subscriptions that ended before today.
issue_title: Status filter contradicts the report
issue_description: Expired subscriptions should not be filtered as `active` if the goal is to find inactive ones.
issue_suggestion: Use the inactive status or remove the contradictory filter.

title: Top categories by product count
description: Return categories with the most products.
code:
SELECT category_id, COUNT(*) AS products_count
FROM products
ORDER BY products_count DESC
LIMIT 10;
issue_title: Aggregation is missing a GROUP BY
issue_description: The query counts all rows together because it never groups by category.
issue_suggestion: Group by `category_id` before ordering the counts.
issue_code:
GROUP BY category_id
ORDER BY products_count DESC

title: First order per customer
description: Show the first order date for each customer.
issue_title: Using MAX returns the latest order, not the first
issue_description: The aggregation direction is reversed for a first-order report.
issue_suggestion: Use `MIN(created_at)` for the earliest order.

title: Distinct customer countries
description: Return each country represented in the customer table once.
issue_title: Grouping by id defeats deduplication
issue_description: Including the primary key creates one group per row instead of one per country.
issue_suggestion: Group only by `country` or use `SELECT DISTINCT country`.

title: Order totals with discounts
description: Calculate the final payable amount after discounts.
code:
SELECT id, subtotal - discount_percent AS final_total
FROM orders;
issue_title: Discount percent is subtracted as a raw number
issue_description: A percent value must be applied to the subtotal, not subtracted directly.
issue_suggestion: Convert the percentage into a fraction of the subtotal.
issue_code:
SELECT id, subtotal * (1 - discount_percent / 100.0) AS final_total
FROM orders;
